import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Migrating a workspace package from one npm scope to another — here
`@restart/{grid,grid-core,bloom-grid,kv-persist,kv-persist-indexeddb,sync}` →
`@papercusp/*` in a sibling internal monorepo — looks like a mechanical
find-and-replace of import statements. It isn't. The imports are the *easy*
references; the ones that bite are the bare strings that no import-grep matches.

## The miss-class: bare package strings in configs

A grep for `from '@restart/x'` / `require('@restart/x')` / `import('@restart/x')`
catches imports and (with a second pattern) `package.json` deps. It does **not**
catch these, all of which name the package as a plain string:

- **`next.config.js` `transpilePackages: ['@restart/grid', ...]`** — Next won't
  transpile the workspace package if the name doesn't match.
- **Astro `noExternal: ['@restart/grid', '@restart/grid-core', ...]`** — SSR
  bundling silently stops including it.
- **`tsconfig.base.json` path maps** — `"@restart/sync": ["libs/sync/src/index.ts"]`.
- **Command / script-runner tables** — `command: 'npm run bench --workspace @restart/grid-core'`
  in a dashboard, a Procfile, a CI matrix. The `--workspace @restart/x` arg fails
  once the workspace is renamed.

<Aside type="caution" title="A running dev server hides all of this">
The dev server cached the old config at boot, so hitting routes that use the
renamed package returns **HTTP 200** even though the configs are stale. Route
smoke checks give false confidence. These references only fail on a **fresh
build** (`next build`, `astro build`, `npm ci` + start) or a dev-server restart.
Verify a scope rename against a clean build, not just the warm dev server.
</Aside>

## The fix: guard on the package pattern, not import syntax

Replace the import-syntax matcher with one that flags **any** `@restart/<pkg>`
occurrence, scanning every line of every code + json file (excluding
`node_modules`, `dist`, the auto-generated `package-lock.json`, and historical
docs). That single pattern catches imports, deps, tsconfig maps, and config
strings uniformly. Make it **targeted** when some names in the old scope are
legitimate (the other app still owns `@restart/{db,ui,shop-sdk,com,...}`): guard only
the migrated basenames, allow the rest. See `scripts/check-no-restart-imports.mjs`
(papercup), wired as a gating CI step. (The other app's equivalent
`scripts/check-no-restart-scope.mjs` was since removed.)

## Bonus gotcha: `grep -v <substring>` self-exclusion

While auditing tsconfig for stragglers I ran
`grep '"@restart/sync"' tsconfig*.json | grep -v libs/sync` to drop the submodule
— and it silently hid the real offender, because the path-map **line** is
`"@restart/sync": ["libs/sync/src/index.ts"]`: the *value* contains `libs/sync`,
so `grep -v libs/sync` filtered out the very line I needed. When excluding the
submodule, match on the file path (`grep -v '^libs/sync/'` against the filename),
never on a substring that can also appear in a line's content.

## Checklist for a scope rename across a monorepo

1. Imports (`from`/`require`/`import()`), incl. subpath imports `@scope/pkg/sub`.
2. `package.json` deps (and the package's own `name`, if it's the one moving).
3. `tsconfig*.json` path maps — `paths` and any project-refs.
4. Build configs: next `transpilePackages`, astro `noExternal`, vite/webpack
   `optimizeDeps`/aliases, jest/vitest `moduleNameMapper`.
5. Command tables / Procfiles / CI: `--workspace @scope/pkg`, `nx run @scope/pkg:*`.
6. Doc-comments and string literals (cosmetic, but a future grep will re-flag them).
7. Relink `node_modules` (`npm install`) so the new scope resolves; then verify a
   **fresh build**, not just the running dev server.
8. Add a gating CI guard so the rename can't silently regress.
